question: Should the default STT provider flip from batch Whisper-small (sherpa) to NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (sherpa-parakeet), and is Parakeet worth adding at all?

criteria_fixed_in_advance.accuracy: mean transcript_score for sherpa-parakeet >= sherpa on the same fixtures (no regression)
criteria_fixed_in_advance.latency: median STTFinalElapsed for sherpa-parakeet <= sherpa (any improvement counts; the fixed floor is vad_silence + pre-roll)
criteria_fixed_in_advance.reliability: no runs without a final transcript; no caption hallucinations on non-speech audio
criteria_fixed_in_advance.decision_rule: flip the default only if all three hold; otherwise ship sherpa-parakeet as an opt-in

sample_transcripts: What is the capital of France? Answer in one word.
What is 2+2? Answer with just the number.
Say hello in exactly three words.
Open the pull request for the Obey Voice repo and summarize the review comments.
What is the capital of France? Answer in one word.
What is 2 plus 2? Answer with just the number.
Say hello in exactly three words.
Open the poll request for the Obey Voice Repo and summarize the review comments.

result.decision: FLIP the default to sherpa-parakeet (tdt-0.6b-v2). Keep sherpa (Whisper) as an explicit choice; add tdt-0.6b-v3 (25 languages) and tdt-110m (small) as parakeet_model choices.

reading_the_numbers: Parakeet transcribed 14 assistant-style utterances x3 with a slightly higher score (0.925 vs 0.912) and finalized ~530 ms earlier at the median (~800 ms at p90). The score differences are real-word wins for Parakeet ('Parakeet', 'Calibre', 'noisy', 'Dr. Patel' vs whisper's 'ParaKeep', 'Caliber', 'nizy', 'doctor. Patel') against two misses ('poll request', 'change log'); both lose the same points on number normalization ('7:45' vs 'seven forty five'), which the scorer does not forgive. Raw decode measured separately through sherpa-onnx-go: Parakeet int8 RTF ~0.025 vs whisper-small int8 ~0.12 on the same CPU (~5x), cold load 0.8 s vs 0.6 s. On the two non-speech fixtures in tests/voiceflow/testdata whisper-small emitted '(Bell)' and '[MUSIC PLAYING]'; Parakeet returned empty — the phantom-turn failure a push-to-talk assistant cannot tolerate. The coreml provider in the prebuilt sherpa lib was also tried: slower than cpu for these int8 models (RTF 0.045-0.10, 3.6 s load), so the engine stays on cpu.
evidence_limits: Fixtures are TTS-synthesized (clean, no mid-sentence pauses, one voice) — they measure decode speed and word accuracy, not endpointing or noise robustness; recorded human speech (just bench record) is still the instrument for those. Score is the benchmark's transcript_score, not WER. Single machine, single run of 3 iterations.
durable_value: Parakeet is the default STT for English installs; whisper-small remains available and protected from models clean while whisper_model is configured; non-English language with an English-only parakeet_model is flagged by doctor.

provenance.fixtures: synthetic (14 utterances, TTS-generated via cmd/golden-tts, 16 kHz mono, 1.5 s trailing silence)
provenance.command: obey-voice benchmark --stt-provider sherpa --stt-provider sherpa-parakeet --iterations 3 --audio-fixture <14 wavs> --expect-text <14 texts> --json-file
